She first gained prominence as a contestant on the American reality television series So You Think You Can Dance in 2016. She signed with RCA Records and gained early recognition for her extended plays (EPs) All the Things I Never Said (2020) and Too Young to Be Sad (2021); the latter became the most streamed female EP of 2021 on Spotify and was preceded by the single " You Broke Me First ", her first US Billboard Hot 100 entry. In 2022, McRae released her debut studio album, I Used to Think I Could Fly , which peaked at number three on the Canadian music charts and was supported by the single " She's All I Wanna Be ". Her second studio album, Think Later (2023), explored a more pop -oriented sound and produced the multi-platinum single " Greedy ", which became one of the bestselling songs of 2024 globally. In 2025, McRae released her third studio album, So Close to What , which topped the US Billboard 200 and yielded the global top-ten hits " Sports Car ", " Revolving Door ", and " Tit for Tat ". That same year, she scored her first US number-one single as a featured artist on Morgan Wallen 's " What I Want " and earned her first Grammy Award nomination for the soundtrack single " Just Keep Watching ". Early life and education [ edit ] Tate [ 1 ] Rosner [ citation needed ] McRae was born in Calgary , Alberta, on July 1, 2003, the daughter of Tanja Rosner, a German dance instructor, and Todd McRae, a lawyer for oil and gas companies who has Scottish ancestry. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] At the age of two, she moved with her family to Oman on account of her father's work; she lived there for three years. [ 6 ] [ 7 ] During her time in Oman, McRae attended The American International School Muscat (TAISM). [ 8 ] McRae began recreational dance training at age six. [ 6 ] [ 9 ] Having returned to Calgary at the age of eight, she began to train more intensively in dance [ 10 ] and competed with Drewitz Dance Productions.
